name: Belgrade
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Belgrade: acquisition and partner diligence, property and procurement risk, and Commercial Court disputes.
hero_lede: Belgrade produces around two-fifths of Serbia's GDP and hosts its banks, technology firms, state enterprises and commercial courts. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching the city, coordinating Serbian counsel and licensed local detectives where on-the-ground enquiries are needed.
intro: Belgrade is Serbia's capital and its dominant business centre, with 1,681,405 residents in the City of Belgrade at the 2022 census. The city accounted for about 40 percent of Serbia's GDP in 2022. Wholesale and retail trade is its largest employer, followed by manufacturing and a fast-growing information and communication sector that includes software outsourcing firms, game studios and development centres of international technology companies. National champions such as Telekom Srbija, Elektroprivreda Srbije, Air Serbia and Delta Holding are headquartered here, as are most banks and insurers, and regional offices of foreign groups use Belgrade as a base for the Western Balkans.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Belgrade because many of Serbia's largest transactions, procurement decisions and disputes pass through it. Foreign acquirers and lenders need to understand who controls private groups that may hold assets across the former Yugoslav region; technology buyers want assurance about the founders, IP ownership and outsourcing relationships of Belgrade software firms; and investors in construction and real estate face questions about permits, land rights and politically connected counterparties. State-owned companies and public contracts concentrated in the capital raise procurement and integrity questions. The city's specialised commercial courts and arbitration institutions are the usual forums when such questions turn into disputes.

matters.title: Private group acquisition diligence
matters.text: Belgrade-based groups often hold companies and property across Serbia and neighbouring states. We map ownership through Business Registers Agency and beneficial ownership records, then add litigation, media and regional registry research to identify related parties, political exposure and undisclosed liabilities before a transaction.

matters.title: Software and IT outsourcing partners
matters.text: Belgrade's ICT sector includes many outsourcing and product companies. We examine founders, ownership changes, IP and employment-related disputes, related entities abroad and reputational issues so clients understand who they are contracting with and whether key assets sit where they are said to.

matters.title: Real estate and construction counterparties
matters.text: Large residential and commercial developments in Belgrade involve investors, contractors and landowners whose rights and connections can be contested. We review corporate and cadastre information through counsel, litigation and media to test ownership, permit history and the track record of developers and contractors.

matters.title: Public procurement and state enterprises
matters.text: Contracts with state-owned enterprises and public bodies based in the capital attract integrity risk. We research bidders, subcontractors and intermediaries, their ownership and links to public officials, and prior procurement disputes, to support compliance reviews and responses to allegations.

matters.title: Asset research for Belgrade disputes
matters.text: Creditors bringing claims before the Commercial Court in Belgrade or arbitral tribunals need to know what assets and connected entities a debtor controls. We map companies, registered pledges, property and regional holdings so Serbian counsel can plan security measures and enforcement.

local_context.title: Commercial Court in Belgrade
local_context.text: The Commercial Court in Belgrade, at Masarikova 2, is a specialised court listed by the Supreme Court of Serbia among the courts of special jurisdiction. It hears commercial disputes between businesses and, in its territory, related corporate and insolvency matters, which makes it the principal first-instance forum for company disputes in the capital. Appeals from Serbia's commercial courts go to the Commercial Appellate Court, which also sits in Belgrade. Court proceedings are conducted in Serbian, and documents in other languages require certified translation.

local_context.title: Arbitration in Belgrade
local_context.text: The Belgrade Arbitration Center, founded by the Serbian Arbitration Association, began operating in January 2014 as Serbia's first arbitration institution not established by the state. It accepts domestic and international cases and lets parties choose arbitrators subject to Board confirmation. The longer-established arbitration institutions attached to the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Serbia are also based in Belgrade. Many cross-border contracts with Serbian parties choose one of these institutions or foreign seats.

local_context.title: Registries and property records
local_context.text: Serbia's Business Registers Agency (APR) is headquartered in Belgrade and keeps the public company register, the Central Register of Beneficial Owners, financial statements and the pledge register, all searchable online. Real estate rights in Belgrade are recorded in the national real estate cadastre maintained by the Republic Geodetic Authority, whose extracts show owners and encumbrances by parcel. Cadastre searches and interpretation of building and permit history are normally carried out with Serbian counsel.

local_context.title: Regulators and licensed detectives
local_context.text: The National Bank of Serbia, which supervises banks, insurers and payment institutions, and the Securities Commission are based in Belgrade, and their registers and enforcement notices are useful sources for financial counterparties. Private detective work in Serbia requires a licence from the Ministry of Interior under the Law on Detective Activity, so any fieldwork in Belgrade is carried out by licensed local detectives and assessed against data protection law.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Belgrade and works on Belgrade matters from Nashville. We agree the purpose with the client and its Serbian counsel first, whether an acquisition, a technology partnership, a construction or procurement relationship, or a dispute before the Commercial Court or an arbitral tribunal, and scope the work to it. Desk research draws on APR company, beneficial ownership, financial statement and pledge registers, court information, regulator registers and Serbian-language media, read by Serbian speakers. Cadastre extracts are obtained through counsel. Any fieldwork is carried out by detectives licensed by the Ministry of Interior, within Serbian data protection law. Reports state sources and confidence levels.

faqs.q: Which court hears company disputes in Belgrade?
faqs.a: Commercial disputes between businesses in Belgrade are heard at first instance by the Commercial Court in Belgrade, a specialised court that also deals with related corporate and insolvency matters. Appeals go to the Commercial Appellate Court, also in Belgrade. Parties may instead agree to arbitration, for example at the Belgrade Arbitration Center. Counsel advises on the forum.

faqs.q: Can we see who ultimately owns a Belgrade company?
faqs.a: Often yes. The Business Registers Agency publishes company founders and members with their shares and maintains a Central Register of Beneficial Owners that can be searched by registration number. Where owners are foreign holding companies, we extend research to the relevant foreign registries and test whether the declared beneficial owner is plausible.

faqs.q: How is property ownership in Belgrade checked?
faqs.a: Ownership and encumbrances are recorded in the real estate cadastre maintained by the Republic Geodetic Authority, and extracts show the registered owner and mortgages by parcel. For new developments, permits, legalisation history and pending disputes also matter. We obtain cadastre information through Serbian counsel and combine it with corporate, litigation and media research.

faqs.q: Can TDSC assess a Belgrade software outsourcing partner?
faqs.a: Yes. We review the company's registration, owners and financial statements filed with APR, related entities in Serbia and abroad, disputes involving founders or employees, and media and reputational sources. The aim is to confirm who controls the business, whether it has the capacity it claims and whether intellectual property or data handling raises concerns.

faqs.q: Can investigators conduct surveillance in Belgrade?
faqs.a: Only licensed detectives may carry out detective activity in Serbia, and their powers are limited by the Law on Detective Activity and data protection law. We do not conduct surveillance ourselves. Where observation or local enquiries are justified, we coordinate licensed Serbian detectives and assess the method with counsel before any work proceeds.
